title: Font size and units
learningObjectives: Explain font size and units and apply it in a readable interface.

understand.concept: font-size sets text size. CSS supports px, em, rem, and viewport-related units. rem is relative to the root element's computed font size; em is relative to the relevant element's computed font size and can compound through nesting.
understand.whyItMatters: Relative sizing can respond to user settings and component context. Fixed sizes can become awkward when users enlarge text or when layouts change.
understand.analogy: A font-size unit is a measuring rule: it determines whether text follows the root, its parent context, or a CSS pixel value.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy builds intuition; actual rendering follows CSS layout rules and browser specifications.

explain.narrative: With a 16px root, 1.25rem is 20px. The nested 1.2em text is 24px when its parent computes to 20px.
